title: VIGIL redesign: three directions
request: Full redesign of the VIGIL crew health app: precise and technical, dark default with a designed light theme, glanceable, few taps, plus a first-run tutorial that explains how it works and where to enter things.
ui_type: Functional app (crew tablet and phone PWA)

directions.name: Flight Deck
directions.idea: An instrument panel: one status readout you can read from across the cabin, then every vital as a calibrated gauge against your own baseline band.
directions.tell: It's the health app that reads like a spacecraft display: one glance tells you if you're go or no-go.
directions.theme: Dark (light theme designed as a daylight panel)
directions.type: Display Space Grotesk / Text Inter / Numerals IBM Plex Mono
directions.motion: Signature: on saving a check-in, the status ring sweeps once and the tiles settle into their new state in sequence. Interaction: press-depth on big touch targets. Ambient: none, or a static dot grid only. Scroll: none; the dashboard fits one screen.

recipe.take: instrument-grade labelling: small caps units, tabular numerals, hairline rules
a terminal-green technical accent used only for live state
dark layered panels with precise 1px borders instead of shadows
readouts that change digit by digit, for vitals

directions.original: The Go / Watch / No-go readout: one word and one ring at the top, sized to read at arm's length, with the reason in one line under it. Status always has a word and a shape, never colour alone.

components.name: Product Tour
components.author: laziekiki
components.why: The first-run tutorial: a spotlight walks the crew member across the real status readout, the check-in button and the body map, keyboard driven and reduced-motion aware.

components.name: Segmented LCD Number Ticker
components.author: shadcnspace
components.why: Instrument-style vitals readouts on the tiles (heart rate, SpO2, dose).

components.name: Number Field
components.author: coss.com
components.why: Big +/- steppers so a value can be nudged from yesterday's reading without a keyboard in microgravity.

components.name: Uptime Card
components.author: kokonutd
components.why: A status strip per indicator, one bar per mission day coloured Go/Watch/No-go, which shows a drift at a glance.

components.name: Segmented Control
components.author: ddoemonn
components.why: One-tap mood, stress and sleep-quality scales instead of sliders, accessible as a radio group.

components.name: Dot Grid
components.author: halaska-studio
components.why: A static plotting-grid texture behind the status panel only, like a scope screen; no motion, no cost.

directions.name: Procedure Card
directions.idea: The daily check-in as a NASA-style procedure: numbered steps, one action per screen, a cue card that tells you exactly what to measure and where it goes.
directions.tell: It's the health app that walks you through your check-in like a flight procedure, one step at a time.
directions.theme: Light first (paper procedure), dark designed for sleep periods
directions.type: Display Inter Tight / Text Inter / Step numbers JetBrains Mono
directions.motion: Signature: each step slides in from the right and the step rail fills as you go, ending on a one-screen summary. Interaction: large tap rows with a check mark that stamps in. Ambient: none.

recipe.take: light technical layout with precise type and generous whitespace
editorial numbering and rules that make long content scannable
a clickable progress rail with direction-aware transitions for the check-in
the daily routine as a vertical timeline with now-marker

directions.original: Every input step carries a cue card: what to measure, how (cuff, camera, wearable), and why it matters in space, so a crew member never wonders where a number goes.

references.name: Rerun
references.take: precise light technical type and grid

components.name: Wizard Steps
components.author: ddoemonn
components.why: Turns the long check-in form into 5 short steps (Vitals, Body, Sleep and mind, Symptoms, Review) with keyboard navigation.

components.name: Onboarding Checklist
components.author: chowlol202
components.why: The tutorial as a first-day checklist with coachmarks: do your first check-in, run the reaction test, read an alert, send a report.

components.name: Timeline
components.author: kuratlielia
components.why: The mission day schedule (wake test 06:15, vitals 06:30, exercise 13:00) with a drawing connector to 'now'.

components.name: Increment Slider
components.author: coss.com
components.why: Sleep hours and exercise minutes: drag for the rough value, +/- for the exact one.

components.name: Notice Alert
components.author: corr
components.why: Restrained Caution / Warning callouts in procedure style for each finding.

components.name: Meter
components.author: redrob-labs
components.why: Cumulative radiation dose against the 600 mSv career limit, colour escalating at the app's 50% and 80% conventions.

directions.name: Flight Deck + Procedures (recommended)
directions.idea: A fusion: the Flight Deck's one-glance dashboard for reading your status, and the Procedure Card's step-by-step flow for entering data. Read like an instrument, enter like a checklist.
directions.tell: It's the health app where you see go or no-go in one glance, and the daily check-in walks you through in under two minutes.
directions.type: Display Space Grotesk / Text Inter / Numerals IBM Plex Mono
directions.motion: Signature: the status ring sweeps on save and the tiles update in sequence. Check-in steps slide with a filling step rail. Tutorial spotlight glides between real elements. Ambient: none. Everything has a reduced-motion fallback.

recipe.take: a calm health app that leads with one readiness answer, then detail on demand
spotlight tutorial on the real UI, and a stepped check-in

directions.original: A 'Today' screen with exactly three things: your status word with its reason, the one next action (Start check-in, Run reaction test, or Send report), and the body map. Everything else is one tap away.

references.name: Rerun
references.take: light theme precision for the daylight variant
